section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch4 — Vygotsky's Sociocultural Theory
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: A young child solving a puzzle is heard talking aloud to herself — 'this piece goes here... no, try that corner' — guiding her own actions through self-directed speech. Vygotsky called this:

options.option_text: Egocentric speech (in Piaget's sense, a meaningless immature stage)

explanation: Vygotsky viewed children's self-talk as 'private speech' — a functional tool for self-regulation and thinking, gradually internalised into silent inner speech — in contrast to Piaget, who saw the same behaviour as meaningless 'egocentric speech' reflecting cognitive immaturity.
